title: Columned Nested List Changed to Vertical List

illustrates.quote: Nested lists are always transcribed in a single column. (See Sample 8-11: Columned Nested List Changed to Vertical List on page 8-24.)

blocks.features: Three side-by-side column headings (Size, Shape, Behavior), each with its own indented sub-items beneath it.

print.notes: Items given in print's left-to-right column order, then top-to-bottom within each column.
print.printFeatures: Styled heading above three side-by-side column headings, each with its own bulleted-looking but unbulleted indented sub-list beneath it.

braille.notes: Print's three side-by-side column headings (Size/Shape/Behavior), each with its own indented sub-items, are transcribed as a single nested vertical list: main entries (Size, Shape, Behavior) begin cell 1 and their sub-items begin cell 3, in print left-to-right column order, per 8.5.1.d — nested lists are never kept in side-by-side columns, unlike simple lists. Line 1 carries the heading plus a trailing reference code; line 2 is blank.

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. Heading level: BOTH runs’ own "level" fields were unreliable (A: null; B: literal "5", contradicted by B’s OWN braille.notes prose calling it "the centered heading") — resolved by direct measurement: source .txt (line 6358) shows 13 leading U+2800 blank cells before ",bird+ ,basics", matching the centring formula floor((40−14)/2)=13 exactly (not the fixed 4/6 of cell-5/cell-7) — level 1 (centred). Nested-list structure (Size/Shape/Behavior main entries, single vertical column per 8.5.1.d) kept as A had it.
